sections.html:
In Abilene, Taylor Central Appraisal District values every parcel in the county. The city, county, school district and other taxing units each set their own rate. The district controls market value only. It has no say over rates or the final bill.

The district office is at 1534 S Treadaway Blvd, Abilene, open weekdays during business hours. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1800, and the phone is (325) 676-9381. A drop box in front of the building takes forms. Send exemption forms to exemptions@cadtx.org and protest forms to arbprotest@cadtx.org.

After a sale, the district learns of the new owner when the deed is filed with the county clerk. Giving the district the recorded document number, or emailing a scan to customerservice@cadtx.org, speeds up the ownership change.

sections.h2: The city tax rate for fiscal 2027
sections.html:
Abilene's council set the city rate at 74.95 cents per $100 of taxable value, a hair under the prior 75.06 cents, when it approved the $414.6 million operating budget on Sept. 10, 2026. The fiscal year starts Oct. 1.

A lower rate does not mean a smaller bill for everyone. The city estimates an average 4.2 percent tax increase on existing property because values rose, and new construction accounts for $16.8 million of the $18.3 million increase in total property tax revenue. The adopted rate also raises more maintenance and operations revenue than the year before.

City of Abilene fiscal 2027 changes
ChargeFiscal 2027 change
City property tax rate74.95 cents per $100 taxable value (prior 75.06)
Average tax change on existing propertyIncrease of 4.2 percent, city estimate
Water and sewer ratesUp 6 percent
Residential solid wasteUp 2 percent
Residential stormwaterUp 10 to 11 percent

The county, school district and other units add their own lines to your bill, so the city rate is only part of the total.

Bills go out in October and are payable on receipt, though most owners can wait until Jan. 31 without penalty. Whatever is unpaid on Feb. 1 is delinquent, and a six percent penalty and one percent interest hit that same day.

The penalty rises a point each month until July 1, when it reaches 12 percent, and interest keeps running at a point a month. A unit that uses a collection attorney can add up to 20 percent more. Seniors and disabled homeowners can split a homestead bill into four payments, and some collectors offer plans of up to 36 months on a delinquent residence homestead.

If you plan to sell, pay before Feb. 1 when you can. Penalties and interest are a cost that falls on whoever holds title when they accrue, and a title company will want the account clear.

A home you own and live in on Jan. 1 qualifies for the general homestead exemption, and filing costs nothing. You do not need to hire anyone to file it, and you do not reapply each year unless the district asks in writing or you move.

  • Turning 65: the extra exemption is added on its own when the district already has your birth date, and applying at any point in that year earns the full year.
  • Mobile home on land you do not own: include the title or a verified purchase contract.
  • Home with a business inside: a homestead apportionment may be available.
  • Nonprofits: federal tax-exempt status does not bring an automatic exemption, and applications are due by April 30.

Texas law has school districts take $140,000 off a homestead, with a further $60,000 for older or disabled owners. Disabled former service members use a separate sliding scale, and a 100 percent rating brings a total exemption.

You can protest market value only. Assessed value comes from a formula and cannot be protested, and a high bill caused by a high rate is not a protest ground. Notices of appraised value go out by April 1 or soon after. The deadline is normally May 31, or a month after the notice arrives if that is later, and each notice prints its own cutoff.

File by mail, email, the drop box or the online portal. The district may offer an informal meeting with an appraiser first, and agreeing to a value there ends the case. Otherwise the formal hearing takes place at the Treadaway Boulevard office, with notice at least 15 days ahead.

  • Bring paper copies of comparable sales, a recent purchase price and photos of defects.
  • Expect three to five minutes per side and about 15 minutes in the room.
  • One postponement is allowed if no agent represents you.
  • Skipping the hearing gets the protest dismissed, and you have four days to ask for a reopening.

Landlords and small business owners also deal with the district's business personal property side. Renditions listing furniture, equipment and inventory are due by April 15. An extension to May 15 needs a written request by April 15, and skipping the filing brings a 10 percent penalty on the taxes ultimately imposed. Rendition forms are on the district's Forms page.

Further appeals go to district court, binding arbitration or, for values above $1 million, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

The county's lien for the year attaches on January 1, so a sale later in the year still carries that year's bill. The title company normally pays it out of your proceeds. Buyers should confirm which exemptions are on the account before closing.

New owners can claim their own homestead for the rest of the tax year if the previous owner did not. The 10 percent yearly limit on assessed value begins the year after an exemption is first granted, so the new owner's clock starts fresh.

Here is a practical order of steps for a seller. Ask the title company early which tax year is unpaid. Pay anything delinquent so penalties stop, or authorize payment from proceeds. Give the appraisal district the recorded deed number after closing so the new owner's name appears on the account. A cash buyer can close quickly, and the title company still clears the tax lien at the table.

faqs.q: Who sets the property tax rate in Abilene?
faqs.a: Each taxing unit does. Abilene's council set the city rate of 74.95 cents per $100 for fiscal 2027, and the county, school district and other units set theirs. Taylor CAD only values property.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Abilene tax bill?
faqs.a: Not the bill itself. You can protest market value with Taylor CAD, normally by May 31 or a month after your notice. The rate is outside its control.

faqs.q: Where is the Taylor Central Appraisal District?
faqs.a: It is at 1534 S Treadaway Blvd, Abilene, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1800, Abilene, TX 79604-1800. The phone is (325) 676-9381, and hours are weekdays 8 am to 5 pm.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for my homestead exemption each year?
faqs.a: No. It continues unless the chief appraiser asks for a new application in writing or you move.

faqs.q: When do Abilene taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: On Feb. 1, so pay by Jan. 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest start that day.
